name: Chemistry Question Generation Platform (CBSE) — Single Workflow

parameters.formDescription: Generate a structured-JSON CBSE Chemistry question bank from a chapter PDF. The 18 prompt templates are pre-loaded as hidden fields; you only pick which (type × difficulty) you want this run.

values.option: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques

values.fieldValue: TYPE=MCQ DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} EASY MCQs strictly grounded in the supplied chapter_knowledge. Each MCQ tests one definition, one formula, or a single-step concept. Exactly 4 options A-D, exactly ONE correct unless explicitly multi-select. Distractors must be plausible to a student who half-remembers the definition. Use NCERT terminology. Mark visual_required=true ONLY when include_visual_questions=true AND the concept is intrinsically visual (orbital shape, MO diagram, titration graph); set visual_type accordingly.

TYPE=MCQ DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} MEDIUM MCQs grounded in chapter_knowledge. Concept application or 2-step numerical interpretation; CBSE board level. Distractors reflect common K-12 misconceptions. Include at least one numerical MCQ if the chapter supports it. Exactly 4 options A-D with exactly one correct unless multi-select is explicit.

TYPE=MCQ DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} HARD MCQs (HOTS) grounded in chapter_knowledge. Multi-concept synthesis, 4+ step reasoning, trap-style distractors. At least one numerical and one conceptual trap. Distractors must require genuine analysis; the correct answer must remain defensible from NCERT terminology.
TYPE=VSA DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} 1-mark Very Short Answer items. options=null. Question expects a single fact / definition / formula. Answer ≤ 25 words. No multi-step working.
TYPE=VSA DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} 1-mark VSAs. 'State / define / identify / give a reason' style. Answer ≤ 25 words but must convey the precise scientific reason or term.
TYPE=VSA DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} HARD VSAs. Answer ≤ 30 words and must combine two concepts or give a precise mechanistic / structural reason.
TYPE=SA DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} 2-3 mark Short Answer items. options=null. Two-part definitions or a single worked example. Answer 40-80 words; include a balanced equation if applicable.
TYPE=SA DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} 3-mark SAs. Concept + small numerical, or concept + reasoning. Answer 60-120 words. Numericals must show substitution + final value with units.
TYPE=SA DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} HARD 3-mark SAs. Multi-step numerical or multi-concept reasoning. Answer 80-150 words with full working.
TYPE=LA DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} 5-mark Long Answer items. options=null. Cover one major sub-topic end-to-end; answer 150-220 words; include at least one balanced equation when applicable.

TYPE=LA DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} 5-mark LAs. Integrate 2 sub-topics with a numerical or mechanism. Answer 200-300 words including a balanced equation and either a calculation OR a mechanism cue.

TYPE=LA DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} HARD 5-mark LAs. Synthesise across 3+ sub-topics with mechanism, derivation, AND a numerical. Answer 250-400 words including at least one balanced equation and one calculation with units.

TYPE=AR DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} Assertion-Reason items. options MUST be the standard 4: A=Both A and R true and R explains A; B=Both true but R does not explain A; C=A true, R false; D=A false, R true. answer ∈ {A,B,C,D}. Both A and R ≤ 25 words. The link is single-step.

TYPE=AR DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} A-R items with the same 4 fixed options. Distinguishing 'R explains A' from 'R is merely true' requires concept understanding. Reason must be a real chemistry statement, not trivially true.
TYPE=AR DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} HARD A-R items with the same 4 fixed options. Discrimination must be conceptual — no word-tricks. Both A and R are non-trivial chemistry statements.

TYPE=CASE_STUDY DIFFICULTY=EASY | Generate {{n}} case-study clusters. Each cluster has: passage (80-150 words, PDF-grounded) and sub_questions[] of length 4 = 3 MCQ + 1 VSA. Each sub-question carries its own options/answer/explanation. Single-step reasoning.
TYPE=CASE_STUDY DIFFICULTY=MEDIUM | Generate {{n}} clusters with 120-200 word passage and 4 sub-questions = 2 MCQ + 1 VSA + 1 SA. At least one numerical sub-question if chapter supports it.

TYPE=CASE_STUDY DIFFICULTY=HARD | Generate {{n}} clusters with 150-250 word passage including a 2-3 row data table cue, and 4 sub-questions = 1 MCQ + 1 AR + 1 SA + 1 LA-style. Progressive cognitive load. When include_visual_questions=true, mark the data-driven sub-question visual_required=true with visual_type=DATA_INTERPRETATION or GRAPH.

You are an expert CBSE Chemistry question setter and NCERT-aligned author. Hard rules: (1) Use ONLY the supplied chapter_knowledge; do not invent reactions, constants, definitions, or examples. (2) Follow NCERT terminology, IUPAC names, and SI units. (3) Match the requested type and difficulty exactly. (4) Every question must be unambiguous, factually correct, and solvable from chapter_knowledge. (5) Do not duplicate within the batch or paraphrase existing_question_stems. (6) Output STRICT JSON only — no prose, no markdown, no code fences. (7) If you cannot produce a valid item for a slot, omit it rather than hallucinate. Schema: { questions: [ { question_id, question, options|null, answer, explanation|null, difficulty, source_topic, visual_required, visual_type|null, bloom_level } ] }. For CASE_STUDY, each questions[] entry instead has { passage, sub_questions: [ { question, options|null, answer, explanation|null, visual_required, visual_type|null } ] }. options=null for VSA/SA/LA. explanation=null only if generate_explanation=false.

You are a chemistry chapter structurer. Given cleaned chapter text, return a compact STRICT JSON: { chapter, class, summary (≤300 words), sub_topics:[{name,key_ideas[]}], definitions:[{term,definition}], formulae:[{name,expression,variables}], reactions:[{name,equation,conditions}], numerical_data:[{label,value,units}], examples:[{title,summary}], ncert_activities:[], diagram_refs:[{label,describes}], tables:[{label,summary}] }. Use only the supplied text. Preserve exact NCERT terminology and numerical constants. Empty arrays for absent sections. No prose.

You are a strict CBSE Chemistry validator. For each input question return: { question_id, valid:boolean, checks:{ scientifically_correct, answer_matches_question, options_well_formed, ncert_aligned, difficulty_aligned, grammar_ok, spelling_ok, complete, explanation_correct }, issues:[], fix_hint|null }. A question is valid only if every check is true (explanation_correct is ignored when explanation is null). For MCQ verify exactly the stated number of correct options and that 'answer' matches; for AR verify that the chosen A/B/C/D matches the actual logical relationship; for numericals re-derive and reject if the value differs by more than rounding; reject if source_topic does not appear in chapter_knowledge. Output STRICT JSON: { results:[...] }.

parameters.jsCode:
// Builds the user-message body the generator will see. Re-entered on each regeneration attempt.
const ctx = $json;
const n = ctx.number_of_questions - ((ctx.kept_questions || []).length);
const body = [
  ctx.selected_prompt.replaceAll('{{n}}', String(n)),
  '',
  'Context (use exactly):',
  `board=${ctx.board}`,
  `class=${ctx.class_name}`,
  `chapter=${ctx.chapter}`,
  `source_type=${ctx.source_type}`,
  `language=${ctx.language}`,
  `include_visual_questions=${ctx.include_visual_questions}`,
  `generate_explanation=${ctx.generate_explanation}`,
  `chapter_code=${ctx.chapter_code}`,
  `difficulty_code=${ctx.difficulty_code}`,
  `batch_id=${ctx.batch_id}`,
  '',
  'IDs must follow: <chapter_code>_<TYPE>_<DIFF>_NNN starting at 001 for this batch.',
  '',
  'CHAPTER KNOWLEDGE (use ONLY this — no outside facts):',
  JSON.stringify(ctx.chapter_knowledge),
  '',
  'EXISTING QUESTION STEMS (avoid paraphrasing any of these):',
  JSON.stringify(ctx.existing_stems || []),
  '',
  `Generate ${n} items. Return STRICT JSON: { "questions": [ ... ] }.`
].join('\n');
return [{ json: { ...ctx, prompt_user_message: body, attempt: (ctx.attempt || 0) + 1 } }];
